issues.title: Some armor adds no armor when worn
issues.effect: Some armor pieces, such as Leather Pants and the Velosian Plume-helm, add no armor when worn and do not lower the damage you take, although their tooltips show an armor value.
steps: Take off all armor and open the character sheet. Armor shows 0.
Hover Leather Pants in the inventory. The tooltip shows ARMOR: 4.
Equip Leather Pants. Armor on the character sheet still shows 0.
issues.expected: Armor rises by the value the tooltip shows.
issues.observed: Armor on the character sheet stays at 0.
issues.cause: Equipping looks up the piece's row of ArmorDataTable by its English name without spaces and apostrophes. No row has that name, for example because the Velosian Plume-helm keeps its hyphen while its row is named VelosianPlumehelm, so the piece counts as Unarmored with no armor. Damage taken is multiplied by 1 minus the total armor divided by 100. The tooltip shows the item's ItemInfo.Damage instead, or the row whose armor name equals the item's name.

issues.title: Amulets and support items show armor they never add
issues.effect: Some amulets and support items, such as Bonecaller's Band and Pactborn Wings, show an armor value in their tooltips but add no armor when worn.
steps: Equip a piece of body armor and note Armor on the character sheet.
Hover Bonecaller's Band in the inventory. The tooltip shows ARMOR: 1.
Equip Bonecaller's Band. Armor on the character sheet does not change.
issues.expected: Armor rises by the value the tooltip shows, or the tooltip shows no armor.
issues.observed: Armor on the character sheet stays the same.
issues.cause: The armor total adds up the head, torso, arms, legs, knee, feet and shoulder slots only. The tooltip shows the row of ArmorDataTable whose armor name equals the item's name, whatever slot the item is worn in.

issues.title: Knee armor counts only after another piece is equipped
issues.effect: Knee armor, such as Broad Knee Guards, adds no armor when it is the last armor you equip. It counts once you equip another armor piece.

itemNotes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Armo: Broad Knee Guards' 7 armor counts only after you equip another piece of armor.
Standard Cap Guards' 6 armor counts only after you equip another piece of armor.

issues.workaround: Equip another armor piece after the knee armor.
steps: Take off all armor. Armor on the character sheet shows 0.
Equip Broad Knee Guards, which add 7 armor. Armor still shows 0.
Equip a weapon. Armor still shows 0.
Equip Feral Maw, a helmet that adds 1 armor. Armor shows 8.
issues.expected: Armor shows 7 once the knee guards are equipped.
issues.observed: Armor stays at 0 until another armor piece is equipped, and then includes the knee guards.
issues.cause: Equipping armor in every other slot recalculates the armor total through Set player Speed based on Armor, which calls Retrieve Player Armor. The knee branch of Attach Equipment attaches the knee armor without that call, so the total keeps its old value until another armor piece is equipped.

issues.title: Some foods do nothing when eaten
issues.effect: Steak, Soup, Turkey Leg, Cooked Red Wrangler, Red Wrangler Sandwich and Potato Seeds are used up without any effect when eaten, although their descriptions promise healing.

itemNotes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Stea: Despite its description, Steak restores no health when eaten.
itemNotes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Soup: Despite its description, Soup restores no health when eaten.
itemNotes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Tuke: Despite its description, Turkey Leg restores no health when eaten.
itemNotes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Craf: Despite its description, Cooked Red Wrangler restores no stamina or health when eaten.
itemNotes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Wran: Despite its description, Red Wrangler Sandwich restores no stamina, health or mana when eaten.
itemNotes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Craf: Despite their description, Potato Seeds restore no health when eaten.

steps: Lose some Health.
Hover Steak in the inventory. Its description says it restores 80 health.
Eat it. The Steak is gone, and Health only keeps regenerating as before.
issues.observed: The food is used up, and Health does not rise beyond its normal regeneration.
issues.cause: Eating looks up the food's row of FoodEffectDataTable by its name without spaces and apostrophes, and then by its localized name. No row matches these foods, so eating applies no effect.

issues.title: Druid's Stew does not boost foraging
issues.effect: Druid's Stew grants Druidsight but not the foraging experience boost it lists.

itemNotes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Craf: Despite its description, Druid's Stew does not boost foraging experience. It still gives Druidsight.

steps: Eat Druid's Stew. The status effects show Druidsight but no foraging experience boost.
Eat Carrot Cake. The foraging experience boost appears.
issues.expected: Druid's Stew adds the foraging experience boost as well as Druidsight.
issues.observed: Only Druidsight appears, and the foraging experience multiplier stays at 1.
issues.cause: The stew's row of FoodEffectDataTable lists the effect as Boost Foraging EXP with a trailing space. The food manager applies effects by name, and no effect has that name.

issues.title: Fairy Staff launches no fireballs
issues.effect: Despite its description, Fairy Staff launches no fireballs and uses no mana.
steps: Hover Fairy Staff in the inventory. Its description says it launches small fireballs each time it is swung and each swing consumes 5 mana.
Equip and draw Fairy Staff with at least 5 mana available. The staff is visible in hand.
Use normal attacks while aiming into open space. The staff swings, but no fireball appears and the mana bar does not drop.
issues.expected: Each normal swing launches a small fireball and consumes 5 mana, as the description says.
issues.observed: Normal swings create no projectile and consume no mana. Charged attacks, blocking and attacks while blocking also produced no fireball in either first-person or third-person view.
issues.cause: The inventory tooltip displays Fairy Staff's ItemInfo.Description, which lists fireballs costing 5 mana per swing. Fairy Staff's Swing Event returns immediately without spawning a projectile or spending mana.

issues.title: Three staves deal 100 damage at point-blank range
issues.effect: The projectiles of Walking Stick, Acolyte Geomancer Staff and Moonstone Staff deal 100 damage instead of 12, 20 and 35 if they hit an enemy as they leave the staff. Attacking from close range can make this happen.

itemNotes./Game/BloodlinesAlpha/Interactables/Weap: Walking Stick's projectile deals 100 damage instead of 12 if it hits an enemy as it leaves the staff. Attacking from close range can make this happen.
Acolyte Geomancer Staff's projectile deals 100 damage instead of 20 if it hits an enemy as it leaves the staff. Attacking from close range can make this happen.
Moonstone Staff's projectile deals 100 damage instead of 35 if it hits an enemy as it leaves the staff. Attacking from close range can make this happen.

steps: Equip and draw Acolyte Geomancer Staff with enough mana to attack and no damage-changing effects active. The staff is visible in hand.
Attack a goblin from a distance where the projectile visibly travels before impact. A normal projectile hit shows 20 damage.
Face a goblin at close melee range and use normal attacks through the second swing of the combo. A projectile that hits as it appears can show 100 damage.
Repeat with Walking Stick and Moonstone Staff. Their distant projectile hits show 12 and 35 damage respectively, while point-blank hits can show 100.
issues.expected: Normal projectile hits use the same base damage at both ranges: 12 for Walking Stick, 20 for Acolyte Geomancer Staff and 35 for Moonstone Staff.
issues.observed: All three staves dealt 100 projectile damage when the projectile overlapped the goblin during creation. At longer range, Walking Stick dealt 12, Acolyte Geomancer Staff dealt 20 and Moonstone Staff dealt 35.
issues.cause: GenericStaffProjectile starts with Damage 100. These three staves call FinishSpawningActor before assigning their literal projectile Damage values of 12, 20 and 35. If the projectile overlaps an enemy during that call, the overlap applies the default 100 before the staff writes its normal value. Whether this happens depends on the projectile's spawn position and the enemy's collision, not a fixed distance.
